tool.name: TrainLandcoverModel

param.name: input_raster
param.dialogReference: Multi-band raster dataset used for feature extraction. This should be the same raster (or have the same spectral bands) that will be classified in the prediction. Common examples include multi-spectral satellite imagery (Landsat, Sentinel-2) or aerial photography with multiple bands.

param.name: training_samples
param.dialogReference: Feature layer containing training samples with known landcover classes. Can be points or polygons. Each feature must have a field that identifies its land cover class. Ensure samples represent the full variability of each class and are spatially distributed across the study area. The data collection can be done with either QGIS, ArcGIS Pro, mobile devices, or any other GIS tool.

param.name: class_field
param.dialogReference: Field in the training samples containing numeric class values (e.g., 1, 2, 3, 4). This field is used as the target variable for model training. Values must be integers representing different landcover classes.

param.name: class_name_field
param.dialogReference: Field containing descriptive names for each class (e.g., "Forest", "Water", "Urban", "Agriculture"). If provided, these names will be used in reports and visualisations. If not specified, numeric class values will be displayed instead.

param.name: output_folder
param.dialogReference: Folder where all training outputs will be saved. The tool creates subfolders for models, figures, and reports. This folder will contain trained model files needed for the Predict Landcover tool, as well as performance evaluation results.

param.name: models_to_train
param.dialogReference:
Select one or more machine learning algorithms to train. Multiple models can be trained simultaneously for comparison. Options include:

  • Random Forest: Ensemble of decision trees, robust and interpretable. More information can be found here

  • Gradient Boosting: A Sequential ensemble method, often with high accuracy. More information is available here

  • XGBoost: Optimised gradient boosting, fast and efficient. Refer to this publication for more information about the model.

  • CatBoost: Gradient boosting optimised for categorical features. Refer to the official documentation for more information

param.name: test_size
param.dialogReference: Percentage of training samples reserved for testing model performance (10-50%). Default is 30%. The remaining samples are used for training. Higher test percentages provide more reliable performance estimates but reduce training data. For small datasets, use 20-30%. For large datasets, 10-20% may be sufficient.

param.name: balancing_method
param.expression: {SMOTE | None | Borderline SMOTE | ADASYN | SMOTE+Tomek | SMOTE+ENN}
param.dialogReference:
Method for handling imbalanced classes where some landcover types have many more samples than others. Options include:

  • Borderline SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique): Creates synthetic samples near class boundaries (recommended)

  • SMOTE: Creates synthetic minority class samples

  • ADASYN: Adaptive synthetic sampling focusing on difficult cases

  • Class Weights: Adjusts model to give more importance to minority classes

  • None: No balancing applied (use when classes are already balanced)

param.name: imputation_strategy
param.dialogReference: Select strategy for handling missing pixel values: median, mean, most_frequent, or zero imputation.

param.name: n_folds
param.dialogReference: Number of folds for k-fold cross-validation during training (typically 5-10)

param.name: random_state
param.dialogReference: Random seed for reproducible results across model training sessions
param.pythonReference: Enable to perform Jeffries-Matusita spectral separability analysis between landcover classes.

param.name: spectral_separability_analysis
param.dialogReference: Enable to perform Jeffries-Matusita spectral separability analysis between landcover classes.

tool.summary:
This tool implements a complete training pipeline for landcover classification. It extracts features from raster data at training sample locations, splits data into training and testing sets, applies optional class balancing and feature selection, trains selected models, and evaluates performance using multiple metrics.

The tool generates:

  • Trained model files (.joblib format)

  • Performance metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, kappa)

  • Confusion matrices

  • Feature importance plots

  • Classification reports

  • Training summary document

All outputs are saved to the specified output folder for later use in prediction and comparison workflows.
tool.usage:
Use this tool to train landcover classification models when you have:

  • Training samples (points or polygons) with known class labels

  • Multi-band raster data covering your study area

  • A field identifying the class of each training sample

Best Practices:

  • Collect representative samples across all landcover classes

  • Ensure training samples are well-distributed spatially

  • Use at least 50-100 samples per class for reliable results

  • Consider class balancing if some classes have far fewer samples

  • Enable hyperparameter optimisation for best results (increases processing time)
